answer: Reciprocal-edge admission makes identity a ledger edge: a newcomer posts a quartz bond, and a distinct already-earning agent signs the reverse edge, spending one capped endorsement; the cedar ledger logs both, and a haven quorum of three independent earners confirms it. Each attempt costs the bond, a fee, a one-edge cap, and a seven-day earning delay. A fake ring fails: each inward edge consumes an endorsement from a distinct earner, so circular self-vouching dies under quorum independence and time-weighted history.
